newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross plans 50,000T food aid to North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross plans 50,000T food aid to North.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross will offer a further 50,000 tonnes of food aid to North Korea during talks in Beijing on Wednesday, a South Korean Red Cross official said in Seoul.

"Our delegates plan to tell their North Korean counterparts that an additional 50,000 tonnes of food would be available for delivery by the end of October," the official said, asking not to be identified.
Red Cross officials from North and South Korea met in Beijing on Wednesday to discuss more food aid to the hunger-stricken communist state.

The southern Red Cross, the only legal channel for private aid to the North from the South, is due to end shipments of 50,000 tonnes of grain aid to the North by next week under an agreement reached in similar talks in May.
In those talks, the first between the two sides for nearly five years, southern negotiators insisted the grain be clearly labelled as coming from South Korea.

The South, still technically at war with the North since the 1950-53 civil war ended in a truce rather than a treaty, also demanded guarantees the food aid would not be diverted into the hands of Pyongyang's military.
